Assume small-deformation, linear-elastic, homogeneous, isotropic solid mechanics.
Consider a solid circular shaft of diameter d = 30 mm (radius r = 15 mm) and total length L = 1200 mm.
The shear modulus is G = 76923.1 MPa.
The moment of inertia is J = pi*d^4/32 = pi*(30)^4/32 mm^4.
The shaft is fixed (clamped, theta = 0) at x = 0 and free at x = L = 1200 mm.
A torque T2 = -200000 N·mm is applied at x = 400 mm.
A torque T1 = +200000 N·mm is applied at x = L = 1200 mm (the free end).
The shaft is divided into two segments: Segment 1 from x = 0 to x = 400 mm (L1 = 400 mm) and Segment 2 from x = 400 mm to x = 1200 mm (L2 = 800 mm).
Compute the internal torque in each segment using equilibrium (cut-and-balance or reaction-method), noting that the reaction torque at the fixed wall is T_R = -(T1 + T2) = 0 N·mm.
Compute the maximum shear stress in each segment using tau_max = T*c/J where c = r = 15 mm, and report the overall maximum shear stress and its location along the shaft.
Compute the angle of twist at the free end (x = L) by summing phi_i = T_i * L_i / (G * J) over both segments, using consistent sign convention with the applied torques.
Present all governing relations (equilibrium of internal torque per segment, tau = T*r/J, phi = TL/(GJ)) clearly in the solution.
Report numerical results with units (N·mm, MPa, rad or degrees as appropriate).
